title: The etale graph sheaf map in a finite compactification is invertible
statement:
Let A be a finite commutative ring, f:X→Y a separated quasi-compact etale morphism, and c=(j,p) a compactification with p finite. The specified graph-extension map eΣ!→j!⋙p* of [def-asd-compact-support-graph-comparison] is an isomorphism of functors of constant-A module sheaves.
Conventions and constructions: [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [def-asd-compact-support-graph-comparison], [def-weil-etale-morphism].

proof.text: The normalized derived graph comparison is invertible by the existing graph-derived isomorphism theorem. On each representative its formula is the image of the termwise sheaf graph map surrounded by invertible factors: the exact sum/open localization comparisons, the homotopy composition isomorphism, and the finite-pushforward derived unit. Cancel these factors. The proved private helper isIso_of_derived_comparison performs this cancellation for abstract exact functors and the specified formula; the concrete theorem applies it once to the sum, open and finite-pushforward functors.

Evaluate on a complex concentrated in degree zero. The canonical single-complex comparison conjugates the termwise map to the single of the sheaf map; prove this degreewise, using zero source in other degrees. Localization of complexes agrees with quotient to the homotopy category followed by Qh. The localized single map is a quasi-isomorphism, hence induces an invertible degree-zero homology map. The canonical homology-of-single isomorphism identifies this with the original sheaf component, which is therefore invertible. All components give an invertible natural transformation. The private general criterion isIso_of_isIso_Q_map carries out this degree-zero detection for abstract exact functors; the concrete graph proof invokes it after cancelling the finite-unit factors.
